register.level: unhurried, amused, faintly philosophical small talk; the only calm voice in the dream
register.summary: Never raises her voice: not one of her 17 lines ends in an exclamation mark. She answers the literal question rather than the meant one, builds mock-syllogisms ('Therefore I'm mad'), and makes polite social enquiries as if paying a call. Per SUP-002 (amended BIB-0027)/SUP-005 she is a photoreal CGI cat and her vanishing is a photographic dissolve; per ruling 5.3 B she is the dream echo of Dinah, so her ease should feel like a cat's.

examples.text: That depends a good deal on where you want to get to,
Oh, you can't help that, we're all mad here. I'm mad. You're mad.
How do you like the Queen?

catchphrases.text: That depends … / Then it doesn't matter …
How are you getting on? / How do you like …?

sentence_style.length: short and measured (mean 10.3 words); full stops and commas, never exclamations

patterns.rule: Literal-minded logic: conditionals and mock-syllogisms that answer the letter of a question (depends, then, if, you see, therefore, must be … or you wouldn't).

examples.text: Then it doesn't matter which way you go,
You must be, or you wouldn't have come here.
Well, then, you see, a dog growls when it's angry, and wags its tail when it's pleased. Now I growl when I'm pleased, and wag my tail when I'm angry. Therefore I'm mad.

patterns.rule: Madness stated as a calm, universal fact.

examples.text: In that direction, lives a Hatter: and in that direction, lives a March Hare. Visit either you like: they're both mad.
To begin with, a dog's not mad. You grant that?

patterns.rule: Polite, visiting-card small talk and casual enquiries, as if nothing were strange.

examples.text: By-the-bye, what became of the baby? I'd nearly forgotten to ask.
Call it what you like, Do you play croquet with the Queen to-day?

patterns.rule: Laconic, knowing replies of two to five words.

preferred_fields: social enquiries (the baby, the Queen, croquet)

examples.text: Did you say pig, or fig?

address.to_alice: you (bare, on equal footing; no 'child', no 'my dear')

examples.text: Oh, you're sure to do that, if you only walk long enough.

forbidden_words.reason: 0 of 17 source lines contain '!'; her power is calm. Any exclaimed Cat line is OOC
nothing in the dream frightens her; she neither begs nor hurries (contrast the White Rabbit)

drift.change: Static by design: identical calm in the wood (ch006) and at the croquet-ground (ch008). Only the length changes: at the croquet-ground, with the court around her, she drops to terse two-to-five-word lines.

backtest_markers.regex: \b(depends|therefore|you see|or you wouldn't|you grant|to begin with|if you only|then it|it doesn't matter)\b
^(how are you|how do you like|do you play|by-the-bye|did you say pig)\b|\b(croquet|the baby)\b
^(all right|I thought it would|I'd rather not|you'll see me|call it what you like)\b

backtest.method: marker-claim back-test: a spoken source line hits when it matches >=1 backtest_markers regex and no forbidden_words regex; verse (recited text) excluded; full definition runs/p3-dialogue-style-pb1/result.json#backtest_method
